# Approach

My goal is to implement a Global Baseline Estimate recommender in R using my movie‐ratings data. I'll start by loading the ratings into a dataframe. Then I'll compute three key components:\
1. the global mean rating across all observed ratings,\
2. each user's bias (how a user’s average rating differs from the global mean),\
3. each movie's bias (how a movie's average rating differs from the global mean).\
Using the spreadsheet's algorithm, I will predict an unseen rating with `predicted(u, m) = global_mean + user_bias(u) + movie_bias(m)`. Finally, for each user, I will generate predictions for the movies they haven't rated and recommend the movie(s) with the highest predicted score.

The main data challenges will be missing ratings (not everyone watched every movie) and small sample size. I’ll handle missing ratings by excluding `NA` values when computing averages (so they don't distort means). Because the dataset is small, individual outliers can strongly affect user/movie averages, so I'll also sanity-check results (e.g., confirm biases make sense and predicted scores stay within a reasonable range).
